chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from ʿUmar ibn Udhaynah, from a number of our companions, that they heard Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام say:
Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام would not perform salat in the daytime until the sun had passed the zenith, nor in the night after performing the ʿIshāʾ salat until the middle of the night.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: The title of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام, the Commander of the Faithful.
key_terms.الْعِشَاءَ: The ʿIshāʾ salat, the night prayer.
key_terms.تَزُولَ الشَّمْسُ: The sun passes the zenith; midday begins.

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about when Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام would not perform salat during the day and night?
ai.summary: This hadith reports the practice of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام regarding specific times in which he would refrain from performing salat. It is relevant to the jurisprudence of recommended prayers and the regulation of worship times in Shia hadith literature.
